claim: For the deterministic Ricker map \(F_{r,K}(x)=x\exp(r(1-x/K))\) with \(r,K>0\), let \(\mu\) be an invariant Borel probability measure whose support is a compact subset of \((0,\infty)\), and let \(X(x)=x\). Then \(K=\mathbb E_\mu[X]\). If \(\mu\) is non-Dirac, then \[r=\frac{2\,\mathbb E_\mu[X]\,\operatorname{Cov}_\mu(\log X,X)}{\operatorname{Var}_\mu(X)}.\] Consequently the one-time stationary marginal identifies both deterministic Ricker parameters exactly whenever it is non-equilibrium; the equilibrium atom \(\delta_K\) identifies \(K\) but not \(r\). Equivalently, every such invariant law satisfies \[2K\,\operatorname{Cov}_\mu(\log X,X)=r\,\operatorname{Var}_\mu(X).\] For a non-Dirac law this also forces positive mass on both sides of \(K\).
integrity: The first-moment calibration is explicitly treated as prior. The accepted contribution is the second logarithmic-moment covariance identity and the resulting stationary-marginal identifiability dichotomy. The 1954 full text was not inspected, so an unindexed historical occurrence remains a residual risk.
scientific_limitations: Autonomous deterministic Ricker map only; the invariant law must have compact support strictly inside the positive half-line. The growth-rate formula requires a non-Dirac law and does not provide finite-sample or noisy-observation guarantees.
title: Stationary-marginal identifiability of both parameters in the Ricker map
